title: 2023 AMC 10A Problem 25
statement: If \(A\) and \(B\) are vertices of a polyhedron, define the distance \(d(A, B)\) to be the minimum number of edges of the polyhedron one must traverse in order to connect \(A\) and \(B.\) For example, if \(AB\) is an edge of the polyhedron, then \(d(A, B) = 1,\) but if \(AC\) and \(CB\) are edges and \(AB\) is not an edge, then \(d(A, B) = 2.\) Let \(Q,\) \(R,\) and \(S\) be randomly chosen distinct vertices of a regular icosahedron (a regular polyhedron made up of \(20\) equilateral triangles). What is the probability that \(d(Q, R) \gt d(R, S)?\)

solutions.text: Fix \(R.\) Of the other \(11\) vertices, \(5\) sit at distance \(1,\) \(5\) at distance \(2,\) and \(1\) (the opposite vertex) at distance \(3.\) Pick ordered distinct \(Q, S\) from these \(11:\) that’s \(11 \cdot 10 = 110\) pairs. The ones with \(d(R,Q) = d(R,S)\) number \(5\cdot4 + 5\cdot4 + 1\cdot0 = 40,\) so \(P(\text{equal}) = \frac{40}{110} = \frac{4}{11}.\) By the symmetry between \(Q\) and \(S,\) the \(\gt\) and \(\lt\) cases split the rest evenly, so \(P(d(Q,R) \gt d(R,S))\) \(= \frac{1 - \frac4{11}}{2}\) \(= \frac{7}{22}.\) Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: From any vertex of an icosahedron, \(5\) vertices are at distance \(1,\) \(5\) at distance \(2,\) and \(1\) (the opposite vertex) at distance \(3\)
Fix \(R;\) by symmetry \(P(d(Q,R) \gt d(R,S))\) \(= P(d(Q,R) \lt d(R,S)),\) so it equals \(\frac{1 - P(\text{equal})}{2}\)
